paper.title: On the Complexity of Bandit and Derivative-Free Stochastic Convex Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Derivative-free SCO, strongly convex quadratic functions
unmapped: Zeroth-order (noisy function value) queries; noise zero-mean with E[xi_w^2] <= max{1, ||w||^2} (location-dependent second moment bound)
F(w)=w^T A w + b^T w + c with ||A||_2, ||b||, |c| <= 1
Learner knows an upper bound B on ||w*|| and the distance parameter epsilon of Assumption 1
Assumption 1: minimizer at distance >= epsilon from boundary, or queries allowed up to distance epsilon outside the domain
settings.definition_quote: we pick and query a point $\bw_t\in \Wcal$, obtaining an independent realization of $F(\bw)+\xi_{\bw}$, where $\xi_{\bw}$ is an unknown zero-mean random variable, such that $\E[\xi_{\bw}^2]\leq \max\left\{1,\norm{\bw}^2\right\}$. ... the \emph{expected optimization error} $\E\left[F(\bar{\bw}_T)-F(\bw^*)\right]$

unmapped: Zeroth-order queries anywhere in R^d; optimum known to lie in the unit ball
Hard instances use Gaussian noise with location-dependent standard deviation max{1,||w||^2}
settings.definition_quote: there exists a quadratic function of the form $F(\bw)=\frac{1}{2}\norm{\bw}^2-\inner{\be,\bw}$, which is minimized at $\be$ where $\norm{\be}\leq 1$ ... the lower bound holds even if we do not restrict at all the domain in which we are allowed to query

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit SCO, quadratic functions (regret lower bound)
unmapped: Zeroth-order queries anywhere in R^d; optimum in ball of radius 1/2
Hard instances use Gaussian noise with location-dependent standard deviation
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit SCO setting, our goal is to minimize the \emph{expected average regret}, namely $\E\left[\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}F(\bw_t)-F(\bw^*)\right]$

settings.name_in_paper: Derivative-free SCO, strongly convex and smooth functions (lower bound)
unmapped: Zeroth-order queries anywhere in R^d; Lipschitz only over the unit ball, global minimum in the unit ball
settings.definition_quote: there exists a function $F$ over $\reals^d$ which is $0.5$-strongly convex and $3.5$-smooth; Is $4$-Lipschitz over the unit Euclidean ball; has a global minimum in the unit ball

settings.name_in_paper: Derivative-free SCO, decomposable quadratic functions (e.g. ridge regression)
unmapped: Observation is F_hat(w)=R(w)+w^T A_hat w + b_hat^T w + c_hat with known deterministic term R and random A_hat, b_hat, c_hat (structured noise)
Learner knows R(.) and an upper bound B on ||w*||; can query at distance sqrt(d) from iterates
settings.definition_quote: Suppose we can write $F(\bw)$ as $\E[\hat{F}(\bw)]$, where $\hat{F}(\bw)$ decomposes into a deterministic term $R(\bw)$ and a stochastic quadratic term $\hat{G}(\bw)$ ... We assume that whenever we query a point $\bw$, we get $\hat{F}(\bw)$ for some random realization of $\hat{A},\hat{\bb},\hat{c}$.

symbols.eps_dist: distance parameter epsilon in (0,1] of Assumption 1

conditions: F(w)=w^T A w + b^T w + c is lambda-strongly convex with ||A||_2, ||b||, |c| <= 1
T/2 integer and the modified domain contains the origin
tuning: perturbation radius epsilon/sqrt(d) with random sign vector
suffix averaging over last T/2 iterates

source.label: thm:quadup
source.quote: Let $F(\bw)= \bw^\top A \bw + \bb^{\top}\bw+c$ be a $\lambda$-strongly convex function, where $\norm{A}_2,\norm{\bb},|c|$ are all at most $1$, and suppose the optimum $\bw^*$ has a norm of at most $B$. Then under Assumption \ref{assump}, the point $\bar{\bw}_T$ returned by \algref{alg:quadratic} satisfies \[ \E\left[F(\bar{\bw}_T)- F(\bw^*)\right] \leq \frac{4(4+5\log(2))(B+1)^4}{\lambda \epsilon^2} \frac{d^2}{T}. \]

results.notes: Expected optimization error E[F(w_bar_T)-F(w*)]; quantity 'other' since it is not a regret. lambda mapped to alpha (strong convexity).

conditions: Gaussian noise with standard deviation max{1,||w||^2}

source.label: thm:quadlow
source.quote: Let the number of rounds $T$ be fixed. Then for any (possibly randomized) querying strategy, there exists a quadratic function of the form $F(\bw)=\frac{1}{2}\norm{\bw}^2-\inner{\be,\bw}$, which is minimized at $\be$ where $\norm{\be}\leq 1$,  such that the resulting $\bar{\bw}_T$ satisfies \[ \E[F(\bar{\bw}_T)-F(\bw^*)] \geq 0.01 \min \left\{1,\frac{d^2}{T}\right\}. \]

results.notes: Lower bound on expected optimization error. The proof's noise (std max{1,||w||^2}) seems to exceed the stated second-moment assumption max{1,||w||^2}; recorded as stated.

conditions: Gaussian noise with location-dependent standard deviation

source.label: thm:quadlowregret
source.quote: Let the number of rounds $T$ be fixed. Then for any (possibly randomized) querying strategy, there exists a quadratic function of the form $F(\bw)=\frac{1}{2}\norm{\bw}^2-\inner{\be,\bw}$, which is minimized at $\be$ where $\norm{\be}\leq 1/2$, such that \[ \E\left[\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} F(\bw_t)-F(\bw^*)\right] \geq 0.02\min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{d^2}{T}}\right\}. \]

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret; multiplied by T. Regret defined via F (mean function), so pseudo-regret.

conditions: F is 0.5-strongly convex and 3.5-smooth on R^d, 4-Lipschitz over the unit ball, global minimum in the unit ball

source.label: thm:convex
source.quote: Let the number of rounds $T$ be fixed. Then for any (possibly randomized) querying strategy, there exists a function $F$ over $\reals^d$ which is $0.5$-strongly convex and $3.5$-smooth; Is $4$-Lipschitz over the unit Euclidean ball; has a global minimum in the unit ball; And such that the resulting $\bar{\bw}_T$ satisfies \[ \E[F(\bar{\bw}_T)-F(\bw^*)] \geq 0.004 \min\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{d^2}{T}}\right\}. \]

results.notes: Lower bound on expected optimization error; by Jensen it also lower bounds average regret (bandit SCO), matching AgDeXi10 upper bound.

symbols.N_R: bound N on the subgradient norm of the deterministic term R over the modified domain
symbols.A_F2: E[||A_hat||_F^2], expected squared Frobenius norm of the random quadratic term

conditions: Assumption 1 holds; can query at points w_t + r with r in {-1,1}^d
tuning: suffix averaging over last T/2 iterates
